channel.title: Articles — Av. Bayram Can Çapar · ÇAPAR Hukuk
channel.description: Av. Bayram Can Çapar — articles explaining Turkish law, based on statutory texts and decisions of the Turkish high courts. English translations; the Turkish originals prevail.

image.title: Articles — Av. Bayram Can Çapar · ÇAPAR Hukuk

item.title: Turnkey Home Purchases in Türkiye: Off-Plan Sale Contracts, Late Delivery, Withdrawal and Title
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law: when buying a turnkey home from a developer, the form of a pre-paid home sale, who may invoke its invalidity, the forty-eight-month delivery limit, penalty clauses and lost rent for late delivery, withdrawal and rescission, security for payments, linked loans, registration and the competent court, with decisions of the Court of Cassation.

item.title: Unpaid Mediation Settlement Can Open the Way to Suing for the Whole Claim: Turkish Court of Cassation Assembly
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, according to the Assembly of Civil Chambers, where a mediation settlement is conditional on full payment and allows all claims to be sued for in case of non-payment, the whole claim may be sued for after deducting what was paid once an instalment is unpaid; the bar in Law No. 6325 art. 18(5) does not prevent this.

item.title: Revoking a Gift of Real Estate in Türkiye: Conditional Gifts, Grounds and the One-Year Period (TCO 295–297)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, donated real estate can be taken back only on the three grounds in Code of Obligations art. 295 and within one year of learning of the ground; the Court of Cassation strictly requires proof of the condition and of its breach.

item.title: Mediation Completed Before the File Reaches the Competent Court Meets the Precondition: Court of Cassation
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, according to the Assembly of Civil Chambers, where an employment action was filed in a court lacking jurisdiction and mediation was concluded after the decision of lack of jurisdiction but before the file was registered at the competent labour court, the precondition is satisfied; dismissal would breach the right of access to court.

item.title: Is a Heart Attack at Work a Work Accident in Türkiye? Law No. 5510 Art. 13 and Court of Cassation Decisions
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a heart attack suffered by an insured while at the workplace is, as a rule, treated as a work accident under Article 13 of Law No. 5510 in decisions of the Court of Cassation’s 10th Civil Chamber; a heart attack in an employer’s shuttle was also accepted. A heart attack suffered by an insured sent on duty, at a place unrelated to the work, was not. The article covers the conditions, the mandatory SGK application and decisions with dissents.

item.title: Invalidity Pension in Türkiye: Conditions, 60% Loss of Working Capacity and Challenging the SGK Decision
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an invalidity pension requires the Institution’s Health Board to find a loss of at least 60% of working capacity, at least ten years of insurance and 1800 premium days, and a written request after leaving work; no pension is granted if a 60% loss existed before first insurance. The article explains the start of the pension and the objection and court route with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Court of Cassation: Survivors’ Pension Reached by Crediting Days Is Stopped; Recovery Limited as SGK Error
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, in its decision of 18.06.2026 the Court of Cassation Assembly of Civil Chambers held that credited periods do not count towards the 5-year and 900-day route for a survivors’ pension, so stopping a pension granted through credited military service was correct; but since the beneficiaries were not at fault, the pensions paid are to be reclaimed under Article 96/1-b of Law No. 5510, limited to five years and interest-free for the first twenty-four months.

item.title: Court of Cassation: An SGK Fine Not Challenged in Time Cannot Be Disputed in a Payment-Order Action
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, in its decision of 15.12.2022 the Court of Cassation Assembly of Civil Chambers held that an SGK administrative fine is challenged by objecting to the Institution within fifteen days and, if rejected, suing in the administrative court within thirty days; once the fine becomes final because that route was not used, an action against the payment order can raise only payment and limitation.

item.title: Promise to Sell Real Estate in Türkiye: Registration Action, Termination, Limitation and Informal Sales
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law: conditions for claiming registration on the basis of a notarised promise to sell, why unilateral termination is ineffective, the ten-year limitation period and the return of the price in informal sales under corrective justice, with Assembly of Civil Chambers decisions.

item.title: Removal and Protection Orders under Law No. 6284 in Türkiye: Objection and Coercive Detention (Arts. 9, 13)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, preventive measures such as removal from the home under Law No. 6284 are issued initially for at most six months and may be extended; an objection lies to the family court within two weeks and the objection decision is final. The article explains the evidentiary threshold, coercive detention for breach, and decisions of the Constitutional Court and the Court of Cassation.

item.title: Appeals in Afyonkarahisar Cases in Türkiye: Konya Regional Court of Appeal and Regional Administrative Court
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, appeals against civil and criminal decisions in Afyonkarahisar go to the Konya Regional Court of Appeal, and appeals against administrative and tax decisions go to the Konya Regional Administrative Court. This article explains the official basis of this mapping, where the petition is lodged, the time limits and the relevant case law.

item.title: Principal Employer and Subcontractor in Türkiye: Sham Arrangements, Joint Liability (Labour Law Arts. 2, 112)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a subcontracting relationship may be set up for ancillary jobs or for a part of the main work required by operational and business needs and requiring technological expertise; if it is a sham, the employee is deemed the principal employer's employee from the outset, and in a valid relationship the principal employer is jointly liable with the subcontractor. The article explains the conditions, the sham-arrangement criteria, the separate examination of each tender period and the payment of severance pay in the public sector, with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Lack of Informed Consent in Cosmetic Surgery in Türkiye: Surgeon's Liability, Proof, Limitation (TBK Art. 147)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a patient must be informed of the risks, complications and alternatives before a medical intervention; the Court of Cassation's 3rd Civil Chamber places the burden of proving this on the physician or hospital. The article explains the scope of disclosure, the consent form, the classification of cosmetic surgery as a contract for work, limitation periods and when a lack of consent must be raised in the action.

item.title: Resale Price, Exclusivity and Non-Compete in Dealership Agreements in Türkiye: Five-Year Limit (Law No. 4054)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a fixed or minimum resale price removes a dealership agreement from the block exemption, and a non-compete obligation exceeding five years cannot benefit from it. The article explains the 30% market share threshold, exclusivity, usufruct agreements and invalidity under art. 56 of Law No. 4054 with decisions of the Court of Cassation Assembly of Civil Chambers and the Competition Board.

item.title: When a Former Employee Sets Up a Competing Business: Poaching, Trade Secrets, Unfair Competition in Türkiye
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Poaching customers and employees and using trade secrets when a former employee sets up or joins a competing business under Turkish law: unfair competition under Commercial Code art. 55/1-b and d, the duty of loyalty, contractual non-compete clauses (Code of Obligations arts. 444–447), the competent court and the Competition Board's decision on no-poach agreements.

item.title: Claiming from the Guarantee Fund in Türkiye: Uninsured, Hit-and-Run or Stolen Vehicles (Law 5684 Art. 14)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a claim may be made to the Guarantee Fund for bodily harm caused by an uninsured, unidentified or stolen vehicle; the Fund pays up to the cover amounts and, according to Court of Cassation decisions, in proportion to the keeper's fault. The article explains the cases covered, the written application requirement, proof, limitation, cover limits and the Fund's right of recourse with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Debarment from Public Tenders in Türkiye: Prohibited Acts, Periods, Shareholders, Annulment (Laws 4734, 4735)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, those who commit prohibited acts in a public tender or during contract performance are debarred from all public tenders for one to two years, and those who fail to sign the contract for six months to one year; the ban extends to shareholders under statutory conditions. The article explains the forty-five-day decision period, the annulment action and stay of execution, and the debate over appeal routes, with Council of State decisions.

item.title: Unfair Competition by Confusion in Türkiye: Trade Names, Packaging and Domain Names (TCC Arts. 55/1-a-4, 52)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, measures causing confusion with another's business are unfair competition without any registration requirement (Turkish Commercial Code art. 55/1-a-4), and art. 52 additionally allows deletion of a trade name and damages. The article explains the criteria for confusion, packaging, product get-up and domain names, acquiescence and the relationship with registered trademarks, with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: How to Challenge a Zoning Fine and a Demolition Order in Türkiye: Zoning Law No. 3194 Arts. 32 and 42
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an action against a stop-work report, a demolition order and a zoning fine for an unlicensed building is, as a rule, brought within the sixty-day period in art. 7 of the Administrative Procedure Law; in the decisions cited, the actions were heard by administrative courts. The article explains the one-month period to obtain a permit, how the fine is calculated, who is liable and the link with art. 184 of the Turkish Criminal Code.

item.title: Zoning Readjustment under Art. 18 of Law No. 3194 in Türkiye: Contribution Share, Objection, Annulment Action
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under article 18 of the Zoning Law (Law No. 3194), a municipality in Türkiye may merge and re-parcel land and plots without the owners’ consent and may deduct up to forty-five per cent of the pre-readjustment area as the readjustment contribution share. The article explains the scope and limits of that share, the allocation of parcels, posting and objection, the time limit for an annulment action and reversal after annulment, with decisions of the Council of State.

item.title: SGK Recourse Against Employers for Work Accidents in Türkiye: Conditions, Fault, Amount and Limitation Period
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, where a work accident results from the employer’s intent or from a breach of occupational safety legislation, the SGK claims from the employer the payments it has made and the initial capitalised value of the income awarded, limited to what the insured person could claim from the employer (Law No. 5510 art. 21). The article explains the conditions, unavoidability, insured persons not notified in time (art. 23), the inner and outer ceilings, the effect of fault reports, the ten-year limitation period and the competent court, with decisions of the Assembly of Civil Chambers and the 10th Civil Chamber of the Court of Cassation.

item.title: Appeals in İstanbul and Ankara, Türkiye: Regional Courts of Appeal and Regional Administrative Courts
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, this guide explains which regional court of appeal and which regional administrative court hear appeals against civil, criminal, administrative and tax court decisions in İstanbul and Ankara, the official basis of their jurisdiction, and where and when the appeal is lodged. It also shows how the jurisdiction of the Ankara administrative courts over central government acts affects the appellate court.

item.title: İzmir Regional Court of Appeal, Türkiye: Jurisdiction (İzmir, Aydın, Manisa), Appeal Procedure, Time Limits
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: The İzmir Regional Court of Appeal hears appeals against civil and criminal court decisions given in İzmir, Aydın and Manisa. This article explains, under Turkish law and with statutory texts and case law, the official basis of its jurisdiction, where the petition is lodged, the time limits in civil and criminal cases, the transitional rule for files from Muğla and Uşak, the effect of applying to the wrong court and the separate appellate court for administrative cases.

item.title: İzmir Regional Administrative Court: Jurisdiction (İzmir, Aydın, Denizli, Manisa, Muğla, Uşak) and Appeals
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: The İzmir Regional Administrative Court hears appeals against decisions of the administrative and tax courts in İzmir, Aydın, Denizli, Manisa, Muğla and Uşak. This article explains, under Turkish law and with official sources, the courts province by province, the thirty-day time limit, where to lodge the petition, final decisions, the expedited procedure and cassation after Law No. 7589.

item.title: Seized Goods and Vehicles in Smuggling Cases in Türkiye: Release, Confiscation, Objection (Law No. 5607)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a vehicle used in a smuggling offence is, as a rule, seized by an annotation on its register; a vehicle impounded in one of three cases is returned if security equal to its value is delivered to the customs administration within thirty days. The article explains seizure under Law No. 5607, the conditions for confiscating a vehicle, the position of a bona fide owner, liquidation, return of the proceeds and the objection route, with decisions of the Court of Cassation and the Constitutional Court.

item.title: Medical Error in Turkish Public Hospitals: Full-Remedy Action, Prior Administrative Application, Time Limits
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an action for harm caused by medical treatment in a state or university hospital is as a rule brought against the administration, not the physician, as a full-remedy action before the administrative courts, as a rule after a prior application to the administration within one year and in any event five years. The article explains the proper defendant, the time limits in Law No. 2577 art. 13, the competent administrative court, expert reports, non-pecuniary damages and recourse against the physician, with Council of State, Court of Cassation and Constitutional Court decisions.

item.title: Contractor Delay in Flat-for-Land Construction in Türkiye: Delay Damages, Termination, Title (TCO Art. 125)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, when the contractor delays delivery the landowner may await performance and claim delay compensation at least equal to the market rent under art. 125 of the Code of Obligations, or seek termination of the contract by court judgment. The article explains the form requirement, contractual penalty, the 90 percent threshold, settlement in forward-looking termination and title annulment with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Unlawful Processing of Personal Data in Türkiye: Application, KVKK Complaint, Damages, Criminal Code Art. 136
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a person whose personal data has been processed unlawfully first applies to the data controller and, if this fails, may complain to the Personal Data Protection Board within the 30/60-day limits. The article explains administrative fines and actions against them, compensation under general provisions and the offences in Turkish Criminal Code arts. 135–136, with Court of Cassation and Council of State decisions.

item.title: Property Inside the Shore Edge Line in Türkiye: Title Cancellation, Compensation and Legal Remedies
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, the title to land lying on the seaward side of the shore edge line may be cancelled in an action brought by the Treasury, and the owner may claim the loss from the Treasury under art. 1007 of the Turkish Civil Code. The article explains how the line is determined, the objection and the annulment action, title cancellation, compensation claims brought before the title is cancelled, how compensation is calculated, the ten-year limitation period and the competent court, with decisions of the Constitutional Court, the Court of Cassation and the Council of State.

item.title: Appeals from Kütahya in Türkiye: Bursa Regional Court of Appeal and Bursa Regional Administrative Court
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, appeals against civil and criminal judgments given in Kütahya go to the Bursa Regional Court of Appeal, and appeals in administrative and tax cases go to the Bursa Regional Administrative Court. This article sets out the official basis of these links, where the petition is lodged and the time limits.

item.title: Mining Licence Cancellation in Türkiye: Forfeited Security and Fines (Law No. 3213 Arts. 10, 13, 17, 24)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an action against an administrative fine imposed under the Mining Law must be brought before the administrative court within thirty days of notification, and the action does not stop collection; for the cancellation of a licence, on this article’s own inference, the general sixty-day limit applies as a rule. The article explains the grounds for cancellation and fines, forfeiture of the security deposit and the competent court with Council of State and Constitutional Court decisions.

item.title: Trademark Invalidity and Revocation in Türkiye: Grounds, Time Limits, Authority, Non-Use (IPC Arts. 25-26)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a trademark invalidity action rests on an obstacle that existed at registration and is heard by a court, while revocation for grounds arising later, such as non-use, becoming a common name or misleading the public, is requested from the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office. The article explains the grounds of invalidity and revocation in the Industrial Property Code (Law No. 6769), the five-year acquiescence and non-use periods, the non-use plea, the competent authority and the effect of the decision, with Court of Cassation and Constitutional Court decisions.

item.title: Aggravated Fraud via IT Systems and Banks in Türkiye: Penalty and the Line with Theft (TCK Art. 158/1-f)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law: the penalty for aggravated fraud committed by using information systems, banks or credit institutions as instruments (Turkish Criminal Code art. 158/1-f), its difference from simple fraud and its boundary with theft through information systems (art. 142/2-e) and bank card misuse (art. 245); the art. 158/4 reduction added in 2026, effective remorse and the competent court, with decisions of the Court of Cassation's Criminal General Assembly and 2nd Criminal Chamber.

item.title: Lifelong Care Contracts in Türkiye (TCO Arts. 611–618): Form, Duty of Care, Termination, Simulation, Abatement
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a lifelong care contract is invalid unless it is made in the form of a contract of inheritance, before an official and two witnesses. The article explains the duty of care, the termination routes in arts. 616–618 of the Code of Obligations and heirs' simulation and abatement claims, with decisions of the Assembly of Civil Chambers and the Court of Cassation.

item.title: Price-Fixing, Information Exchange and Concerted Practices in Türkiye (Law No. 4054 Art. 4): Fines, Leniency
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, joint price-setting, exchange of competitively sensitive information and concerted practices between competitors are prohibited by Article 4 of Law No. 4054, and the Competition Board may impose fines of up to ten percent of annual gross revenue. This guide explains the presumption of concerted practice, how fines are calculated, and leniency, settlement and commitments, with Competition Board and Council of State decisions.

item.title: Competition Damages in Türkiye: Treble Damages, Proof, Board Decisions, Limitation (Law No. 4054 Arts. 56-59)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, buyers and competitors harmed by an anti-competitive agreement or an abuse of dominance may claim damages under arts. 56–59 of Law No. 4054: invalidity, calculation of loss, treble damages, the presumption in art. 59, the Competition Board decision as a preliminary question, the eight-year limitation period applied by the Court of Cassation and the competent court, with Court of Cassation decisions and an example Competition Board decision.

item.title: Challenging Competition Board Decisions in Türkiye: Administrative Fines, Competent Court and Time Limits
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an action against an administrative sanction decision of the Competition Board is brought before the competent administrative court; the time limit is sixty days from notification of the reasoned decision, and filing the action does not suspend collection of the fine. The article covers the investigation procedure under Law No. 4054, rights of defence, on-site inspections, fine rates, settlement, stay of execution and appeals, with Constitutional Court and Council of State decisions.

item.title: Reserve Building Area Designation Annulment (Law No. 6306): Time Limit and Stay of Execution in Türkiye
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a reserve building area is an area designated by the Ministry for use in implementations under Law No. 6306; an action may be brought before the administrative courts within thirty days of notification against acts taken under the Law. The article explains the definition amended by Law No. 7471, the suspension of zoning procedures, the majority decision, stay of execution and decisions of the Council of State and the Constitutional Court on urgent expropriation.

item.title: Breach of the Duty of Disclosure in Turkish Insurance: Can the Insurer Refuse the Claim? (TCC Arts. 1435–1440)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, if the policyholder fails to disclose material matters, the insurer may withdraw within fifteen days or request an additional premium before the insured event; after the event, the claim is as a rule not refused entirely but reduced or paid proportionally depending on fault and connection. The article explains pre-existing illness in life and health insurance with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Challenging a Deportation Order and a Residence Permit Refusal in Türkiye: Law No. 6458 Arts. 53, 57 and 25
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an action against a deportation order must be brought before the administrative court within seven days of notification; the court's decision is final and, unless the foreigner consents, the foreigner is not deported until the proceedings end. The article explains the challenge to administrative detention before the criminal judge of peace, the entry ban, actions against residence permit refusals, and decisions of the Constitutional Court and the Council of State.

item.title: Company Tax Debt in Türkiye: Shareholder and Legal Representative Liability (Law 6183 Art. 35), Payment Orders
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, the shareholder's proportional liability and the legal representative's duty-based liability for a limited company's unpaid tax debt, the order of enforcement, the relevant period and the 15-day time limit to challenge a payment order, with Constitutional Court and Council of State decisions.

item.title: Arbitration Clauses under Turkish Law: Validity, the Arbitration Objection and Lawsuits Filed in Court
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an arbitration clause must be in writing, the dispute must be arbitrable and, according to the Court of Cassation's Assembly of Civil Chambers, the intention to arbitrate must be clear and definite. The article explains the preliminary objection of arbitration and its time limit where a lawsuit is filed in court in Türkiye despite the clause, separability, domestic arbitration versus arbitration with a foreign element, the annulment action against an arbitral award and interim measures.

item.title: Design Protection in Türkiye: Registered and Unregistered Designs, Novelty, Infringement (IPC Arts. 55-81)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a design is protected as a registered design if registered and as an unregistered design if first made available to the public in Türkiye; in both cases it must be new and have individual character. The article explains the conditions of protection, the twelve-month grace period, terms of protection, infringement and invalidity actions and the relationship with unfair competition rules, with Court of Cassation decisions.

item.title: Copyright Infringement in Türkiye: Triple Fee, Damages, Complaint, Time Limits (Law No. 5846 Arts. 66–71, 75)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, a person whose copyright is infringed may seek removal and prevention of the infringement without proof of fault, up to three times the contractual fee or market value for economic rights, and damages if the infringer is at fault; infringement is also a complaint-based offence with a six-month complaint period. The article explains arts. 66–71, 75 and 76 of Law No. 5846 with decisions of the Court of Cassation Assembly of Civil Chambers and the Constitutional Court.

item.title: Which Court Hears Commercial and Consumer Cases in Türkiye: Muğla, Manisa, Uşak, Afyonkarahisar, Kütahya
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, where there is no commercial or consumer court, the civil court of first instance hears commercial and consumer cases in the relevant capacity, and Council of Judges and Prosecutors Decisions No. 1235 and 1236 set the rule for which numbered civil court hears these cases. This article sets out the position in central Muğla, Manisa, Uşak, Afyonkarahisar and Kütahya, jurisdiction objections, mediation and the arbitration committee threshold, with official sources.

item.title: Short-Term Tourist Rentals in Türkiye: The Permit, Flat Owners' Unanimous Decision and Administrative Fines
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, letting a dwelling for one hundred days or less requires a permit under Law No. 7464, and in a building with more than one independent unit a unanimous decision of all flat owners is required as a rule. The article explains the application, the exceptions to unanimity, the twenty-five per cent cap, the ban on subletting, administrative fines, remedies and the neighbours' rights under condominium law, with decisions of the Constitutional Court, the Council of State and the Court of Cassation.

item.title: Acquiring Turkish Citizenship after Birth: Routes, Conditions and Challenging a Refusal
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, citizenship may be acquired after birth through the general route (five years of uninterrupted residence), marriage (at least three years), the exceptional route, re-acquisition and adoption; meeting the conditions does not give an absolute right. The article explains the conditions in Law No. 5901, the application procedure in Türkiye, the sixty-day time limit, the competent court and how the Council of State and the Constitutional Court review refusals.

item.title: Tax Cases from Uşak, Afyonkarahisar and Kütahya: Which Court, Time Limits and Appeal in Türkiye
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: There is no tax court in Uşak, Afyonkarahisar or Kütahya; tax cases are heard by the Manisa, Konya and Eskişehir Tax Courts respectively. This article explains, under Turkish law and with official sources and Council of State decisions, the venue rule (Law No. 2577 art. 37), the thirty- and fifteen-day time limits, where the petition may be lodged, what happens when a case is filed in the wrong court, and the appellate court.

item.title: Tax Loss Penalty and Settlement in Türkiye: How a Settlement Request Affects the Time to Sue (VUK, İYUK)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, the tax loss penalty is as a rule one times the tax; post-assessment settlement is requested within thirty days of service of the tax notice and, if no settlement is reached, the time limit for an action against the penalty is extended where necessary to fifteen days from service of the record. The article explains the art. 376 reduction, pre-assessment settlement, penalties excluded from settlement and the change made by Law No. 7524.

item.title: Work Permits for Foreign Nationals in Türkiye: Challenging a Refusal and Fines (Law No. 6735 Arts. 21, 23)
item.dc:creator: Av. Bayram Can Çapar
item.description: Under Turkish law, an objection against a work permit refusal may be filed with the Ministry within thirty days of notification, and the administrative courts may be seized if the objection is rejected; foreigners working without a permit and the employers who employ them face administrative fines, and the foreigner is reported for deportation. The article explains the application, refusal, objection and penalty provisions of the International Labour Force Law No. 6735 with decisions of the Council of State and the Court of Cassation.
